answer: The glacier-sable ledge survey binds one identity to one measured ledge: the claimant plants a sable flag on a named glacier ledge, carves a notch at the ice line, and records how meltwater crosses the mark over two tides. Two ledge keepers repeat the measure, check the flag against the sable register, and confirm the reading within five days. A moved flag, a faked notch, or a reading taken off the ledge voids the season, burns a 100-credit stake, and bars the sponsor for two years. One honest survey costs 100 credits; 1,000 fakes need 1,000 ledges climbed, flagged, and read by hand.
